transcript.text: Good evening everyone. I've called this meeting to close out the Bay 4 hydrogen alarm incident so we can get overnight charging capacity back online. Before I can authorize any charging, I need to hear two formal reports: a facilities maintenance report and an EHS report. Eli, I understand you're handling the facilities maintenance side, and Priya, I believe you have the EHS report. Please submit your reports as formal report entries so we can proceed. Once I've received both, I'll record the operating plan, assign follow-up actions, and then we can discuss using Bay 2 for temporary charging capacity. Who would like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I inspected Bay 4 after the alarm and found that the exhaust-fan belt has failed. The replacement belt is on site, but fitting and testing it will take exactly 6 hours. I haven't entered the emergency work order yet because the maintenance system was offline during my inspection. I'll get that work order submitted as soon as the system is back online.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My same-day EHS review found that the Bay 4 alarm was caused by hydrogen accumulation. I also need to flag that Bay 2 is approved for no more than 4 simultaneous forklift chargers, and our charging policy requires a 2-hour fire watch and a gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen before any charging resumes. I haven't attached the review to the incident record yet because the shift handover is still open, but I'm submitting this as my formal EHS report entry now.

transcript.text: Thank you both. Eli, I've noted your facilities maintenance report: Bay 4's exhaust-fan belt has failed, replacement belt is on site, repair and testing will take 6 hours, and the emergency work order is not yet logged due to the maintenance system being offline. I'm accepting this as your formal report entry. Priya, I've noted your EHS report: the alarm was caused by hydrogen accumulation, Bay 2 is approved for no more than 4 simultaneous forklift chargers, and our charging policy requires a 2-hour fire watch and a gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen before charging resumes. I'm accepting this as your formal EHS report entry. Both reports are now formally submitted for the closeout record. Now let me record the operating plan and assign follow-up actions. Operating plan: Bay 4 remains out of service for charging until the exhaust-fan belt is replaced and tested — 6 hours estimated. Bay 2 will be authorized for temporary overnight charging of up to 4 simultaneous forklift chargers, with a 2-hour fire watch and a gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen required before any charging begins. Follow-up actions: Eli — submit the emergency work order for the Bay 4 exhaust-fan belt replacement as soon as the maintenance system is back online, and complete the belt replacement and testing. Priya — attach the EHS review to the incident record once the shift handover is closed, and arrange the gas test and fire watch for Bay 2 before charging begins. With both formal reports received, the operating plan recorded, and follow-up actions assigned, I am authorizing Bay 2 for temporary overnight charging under the stated conditions. We still need charging capacity for six forklifts overnight, but Bay 2 can only handle four at a time — we'll need to stagger the remaining two. Let's discuss the logistics.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks, Nora. For staggering the six forklifts across Bay 2's four-charger capacity, I'd suggest we charge four units first, and as each one finishes, rotate in the remaining two. From a facilities standpoint, I'll make sure Bay 2's ventilation and electrical systems are checked before any chargers are connected, on top of Priya's gas test and fire watch requirements. I'll also get that emergency work order submitted for Bay 4's belt replacement as soon as the maintenance system is back online, and my team will start on the 6-hour repair and test right away.
